fieldNotes.site: Ball Metal Beverage Container can plant at 105 E Blackhawk Dr, Fort Atkinson WI (SE edge of town). Complex = a grey pitched-roof production hall (N) joined to a white flat-roof process hall (S, heavy rooftop equipment). Employee parking to the W; a paved truck apron runs along the E face. 201 E Cramer St (dunnage node) is a separate nearby address, not the plant.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE — a rail spur leaves the N-S mainline and runs into the plant along the east face (rail cars can be spotted for coil-in / can-out). This is the one rail-served site of the five.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Single entrance drive off Blackhawk Dr (at a rail grade crossing) running up the east apron; no guard booth or barrier arm visible. The two small fenced structures on the east apron are UTILITY/electrical compounds (transformers/switchgear), not a gatehouse or truck scale. Classed no-gate/no-guard, flagged medium.
fieldNotes.docks: ~15 dock doors estimated on the east face facing the truck apron (modest external dock bank; some volume moves by the rail spur). Band 10-25.
fieldNotes.dropArea: No dedicated trailer-storage lot; trailers stage on the east working apron -> dropArea 0-10, dropYard false.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Fort Atkinson is a small town (~12k) in Jefferson County; plant on the SE edge with farmland to the N/E -> Rural. Cell coverage fine (not isolated).
fieldNotes.backupNote: The entrance sits at a rail grade crossing on Blackhawk Dr; a long inbound queue could interact with the crossing, but the east apron gives internal stacking room, so not classed backup-sensitive.

citations.claim: Ball's own Feb-2025 locations map lists Fort Atkinson, WI as an operating site.

verification.rationale: Long-running Ball Metal Beverage can plant, confirmed current on Ball's own 2025 locations map; not among Ball's closures.
